research.population_and_history: Verified via Wikipedia: Chestermere had a population of 22,163 at the 2021 census, up from 1,043 permanent residents in the early 1990s. Became a city on January 1, 2015 (previously a summer village from 1977, then a town from 1993). Was 'the fastest growing town in Alberta' pre-city-status.
research.chestermere_lake: Verified via Wikipedia: Chestermere Lake began as a natural wetland developed into an irrigation reservoir around 1907. Today it supports waterskiing, wakeboarding, fishing and other water sports; the Calgary Yacht Club operates there and the city holds an annual Water Festival.
research.neighbourhoods: Verified via a Chestermere real estate community-guide page: established/mature communities include Westcreek (development began 1991), Westmere (most diverse housing mix -- townhouses, villas, apartments, single-family), Lakeview Landing (1999-2005), The Cove (40 lakefront homes, late 1990s), and Lakeside Greens (1991-1998, walkout basements). Newer communities include Kinniburgh, Chelsea, Rainbow Falls (SW, two new elementary schools opened 2008), Waterford, and South Shore (single-family homes from $800k+).
research.triple_garages: Verified via multiple Calgary-area realtor listing pages (calgarylistinghub.ca, mypadcalgary.com, dianerichardson.ca, chestermererealestate.com, forsaleincalgary.com) that triple-car-garage homes are a distinct, actively marketed category in Chestermere new builds -- used this as the direct evidence for the 'blank-box triple garage' angle rather than asserting it without a source.
research.coordinates: Corrected during build: initially estimated latitude/longitude, then verified via latlong.net (51.049999, -113.822502) and updated the LocalBusiness schema to the confirmed figures before publishing.
research.not_used: Declined to cite a specific dyke/reservoir capacity figure, exact lot sizes, or HOA/architectural-control bylaw text since no single verifiable source gave a precise number for any of these -- described the new-build triple-garage pattern and lake lifestyle in general, source-backed terms instead.

runs.word_count: ~2770 total page words (nav/footer/schema included), well over the 1500-word body minimum
runs.why_this_target: Market flipped to Vancouver per alternation (last run 09-16 was Calgary/Chestermere). Audited all ~85 existing .html filenames and titles before committing. garage-organization-burnaby.html and garage-cleaning-burnaby.html already exist, but no storage-solutions-burnaby.html -- this was the clearest, most-repeated recommendation across the last three run logs (09-12, 09-14, 09-16 next_targets all named it as the top Vancouver opportunity, since it mirrors the #2-ranking garage-storage-solutions-calgary.html frozen page). Storage (shelving/racks/bins/wall systems) is a genuinely distinct intent from organization (layout/design) and cleaning, and Burnaby has neither a dedicated storage page nor -- critically -- any competitor page that ties storage material choice to Burnaby's split housing stock or its strata storage rules.
runs.competitive_gap_found: WebSearch for 'garage storage solutions Burnaby' and 'garage shelving Burnaby BC' returned only generic company template pages (Garage Living, Unique Storage & Organizers, Clever Garage, Clever Quarters) with no real Burnaby-specific content -- one competitor's 'Burnaby' page was actually Vancouver content with the city name swapped in. None of them address strata/condo storage rules (a huge gap given Burnaby's condo/townhouse density), none give real climate numbers to justify material choices, and only one namedrops neighbourhoods without any real detail. Built the page around the two things nobody else covers: the tandem-garage one-wall-only shelving constraint, and BC strata law on what can actually be stored in a garage or parking stall.

research.neighbourhoods_housing: Verified via presidentmovers.ca and zealty.ca real-estate guides: Metrotown is high-rise condo/mixed-use with Metropolis mall and Central Park (90 acres, old-growth forest); Brentwood is mostly condos/towers with '250+ shops, 11 new residential towers' around Brentwood Town Centre SkyTrain; Burnaby Heights has heritage homes and post-war bungalows plus historic Hastings St neon signage; South Burnaby/Edmonds is predominantly single-family and townhomes near the Fraser River, Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park and Riverway Golf Course.
research.climate: Two sources (climate-data.org, weather-and-climate.com) give slightly different figures, so used ranges rather than false precision: average annual rainfall roughly 2,300mm+, wettest months Nov-Jan, humidity commonly cited 65-85% depending on month/source.
research.strata_law: Verified via BC government (gov.bc.ca) Strata Housing guidance: garage/parking areas in strata buildings are either common property or limited common property (LCP); strata bylaws can restrict what's stored there (furniture, combustibles); exclusive-use rights attach to the owner, not the strata lot, so they don't automatically transfer on resale; Form B Information Certificate plus current bylaws govern the actual rules for a given building. This is general BC provincial guidance, not Burnaby-specific bylaw text -- described it that way, not as a Burnaby-only rule.
research.not_used: Declined to cite specific real-estate price figures (median condo/townhouse prices) since they date quickly and aren't needed to make the storage argument -- used only the verifiable structural fact (eleven towers around Brentwood) for local texture.
